observations:
Torah #175 contains exactly 7 concepts across one bechina-connected component: בְּכִיָּה, בִּינָה, שֵׁם ס"ג, מִלּוּי שֶׁל ס"ג, לֵב, שִׂמְחָה, and חֶדְוָה. All 7 are accounted for in Package 1 ('בְּכִיָּה וּבִינָה וְשִׂמְחָה') in torah_175_packages.json. No independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists here that would form a separate new package.

The candidates examined for a potential additional or split package are:

(1) A 'Kabbalistic Name Structure' cluster using שֵׁם ס"ג and מִלּוּי שֶׁל ס"ג alone: These two concepts could in principle form a micro-cluster about the Divine Name and its expansion. However, (a) they are already within the unified Binah-heart-joy-weeping chain and are not an independent domain — they are the kabbalistic infrastructure that links בְּכִיָּה to בִּינָה; (b) a 2-node cluster of שֵׁם ס"ג and מִלּוּי ס"ג would be redundant, since מִלּוּי ס"ג is effectively the same entity as שֵׁם ס"ג in expanded form; (c) the framework requires 3+ bechina-connected concepts to justify an independent new package. No new package warranted.

(2) A 'Joy and Delight' cluster using שִׂמְחָה and חֶדְוָה alone: These two form a bechina pair (hendiadys), but a 2-node cluster is too small to constitute an independent new package. The framework's merge rule correctly absorbs this pair into the main cluster via their connection to לֵב. No new package warranted.

(3) A 'Crying and Regret' cluster using בְּכִיָּה and חֲרָטָה: While חֲרָטָה (regret) appears in the teaching, it is an eitza-result of joy — what joy produces. There is no bechina declaration equating חֲרָטָה with בְּכִיָּה or any other concept. A package requires bechina connections; חֲרָטָה has none in this Torah. No new package warranted.

(4) A split of Package 1 into 'Binah/Kabbalistic' sub-package and 'Joy/Heart' sub-package: One could consider whether the kabbalistic concepts (שֵׁם ס"ג, מִלּוּי ס"ג, בִּינָה) form one domain and the experiential concepts (שִׂמְחָה, חֶדְוָה, לֵב, בְּכִיָּה) form another. However, this split would violate the connected-components principle: לֵב is explicitly identified as בִּינָה ('בִּינָה – לִבָּא'), making these two sub-domains inseparable. The teaching's entire purpose is to show that the kabbalistic and experiential domains ARE the same domain — the kabbalistic identity of Binah and the heart IS the reason that joy and weeping share the same locus. Splitting would destroy the teaching's central insight. No split warranted.

Conclusion: Torah #175's complete bechina topology is exhausted by the single 7-node package. The teaching is architecturally unified — its power lies in the chain of identities that collapses the apparent opposition between weeping and joy into a single kabbalistic reality (Binah/heart). No independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists outside this unified chain that would justify a new package.
